title: Phase 6a: replace Postgres '~' regex in GetNextRootCardID (cards.go) — missed Phase 3 PG-ism
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Phase 3's PG-ism inventory checked ARRAY[ and = ANY($1) but NOT the Postgres regex match operator '~'. Two call sites survive:

- services/cards.go:810 — GetNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
- handlers/cards.go:494 — (s *Handler) getNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'

SQLite has no '~' regex operator (REGEXP requires a user-defined function). The query errors silently, returns empty, and GetNextRootCardID falls back to '1' instead of the correct MAX(numeric)+1. This breaks 3 handler tests (TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute, contributes to TestGetNextChildCardID) and is a REAL production bug post-cutover: every new root card would collide on id '1'.

Note these are duplicate implementations (services + handlers both inline the SQL). The handlers copy is the legacy dup; services.GetNextRootCardID is the canonical one (called from handlers/epub.go).

Fix: no cross-driver SQL expresses 'pure digits' (LIKE has no char classes on either DB; GLOB is SQLite-only). Pull the filter into Go: SELECT candidate card_id WHERE user_id/is_deleted, then filter with regexp.MustCompile('^[0-9]+$').MatchString and take the max via strconv.Atoi. At single-user scale this is trivial. Ideally dedupe the two impls onto the services one and have the handler call it.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Blocks the cards-id cluster of Zettelgarden-j89.
acceptance_criteria: GetNextRootCardID works identically on Postgres and SQLite; the '~' operator is gone from services/cards.go and handlers/cards.go; TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; no other PG regex operators remain in non-test Go (grep clean).

title: Phase 6a: handler pool-vs-test-tx write isolation audit (s.DB vs s.GetDB())
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Dominant root cause behind the handlers test failures.

Mechanism: handlers.GetDB() returns the rolled-back per-test transaction (h.Server.Tx) in testing mode, but many handler methods write via the raw pool handle s.DB instead, which COMMITS for real. Reads that then go through GetDB() see a snapshot from before the write -> wrong result. Same mechanism leaks rows across tests (test pollution), since pool writes are never rolled back by Teardown.

Concrete confirmed case: handlers/auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute does s.DB.Exec('UPDATE users SET password = ...'). Then LoginRoute -> QueryUserByEmail (handlers/users.go:411) reads via s.GetDB() (the test tx, snapshot taken in Setup before the reset) -> sees the OLD password hash -> checkPasswordHash fails -> 401. TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess fails on SQLite; on Postgres MVCC the same staleness applies but the suite may have masked it by ordering. Other handlers using raw s.DB.Exec/Query (auth.go:352/383/413/449/475, plus JobRunner wired with S.DB in handlers/setup_test.go) are suspect.

Knock-on pollution (tests that pass in isolation but fail in the full suite because earlier pool-writes leak): TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags, and the 'database is locked' cleanup in TestGetNextChildCardID (pool write during an open tx).

Fix is a systematic audit, NOT a one-line change: route handler writes through GetDB() everywhere a test tx exists; reserve raw s.DB for the few places that genuinely need out-of-transaction access (and make them explicit). Source/JobRunner wiring (setup_test.go) should pass GetDB() too. Verify isolation holds by running the full handlers package (not just single tests).

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Largest lever among the remaining failures (~4-5 of the 11).
acceptance_criteria: No handler write path uses raw s.DB where a test-transaction-aware GetDB() is intended; TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess green on SQLite; cross-test card/prefs leakage (Typesense upsert of card 28, etc.) eliminated; documented convention for when raw pool access is legitimately required.

title: Phase 6a: notification_preferences UPDATE is not an upsert (relies on a trigger that never existed)
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). handlers/notifications.go UpdatePreferences (line ~236) contains the comment 'This is handled by the trigger in the database' — but NO such trigger exists. Migration 0121 only runs a one-time INSERT INTO notification_preferences (user_id) SELECT id FROM users ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; there is no per-user auto-create trigger, and it was never ported to Go in Phase 5 (Phase 5 covered user_stats / llm_jobs / rss notifications, not this).

Consequence: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences does a plain UPDATE ... WHERE user_id = $1. When the user has no prefs row (common — e.g. test users inserted by importTestData, or any user created after the 0121 backfill), the UPDATE affects 0 rows, the handler's 'no rows' retry branch never fires (Exec returns no error), and the subsequent GetNotificationPreferences returns 'sql: no rows' -> handler returns 500 'Failed to get preferences'. This is a latent bug on BOTH Postgres and SQLite, not a SQLite regression.

Fix: make models.UpdateNotificationPreferences an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET ... (works identically on both drivers; the table PK is user_id). Drop the misleading trigger comment and the dead retry branch.

TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess is the failing test. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences is an upsert (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE) or the handler creates-then-updates; works on both drivers; TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess green on SQLite; the misleading 'trigger' comment removed.

title: Phase 6a follow-up: port handlers/facts.go + handlers/entity.go = ANY($1) + array_position to SQLite
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a (2026-07-26). Two production handler sites still use the Postgres array pattern that the services layer was fixed for in the same session:

- handlers/facts.go:808 -- WHERE f.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, f.id), called with pq.Array(factIDs)
- handlers/entity.go:1141 -- WHERE e.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, e.id), called with pq.Array(entityIDs)

The other 7 '= ANY($1)' sites were translated to IN (...) via the new models.InList / models.IntArgs helpers (models/sql.go). These 2 were deferred because they ALSO use 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' to preserve the input-slice order, which SQLite has no equivalent for.

Fix: translate '= ANY($1)' to 'IN ' || models.InList(1, len(ids)) (no fixed scalars here, so start at 1), drop the ORDER BY array_position clause, bind via models.IntArgs(ids)..., then reorder the scanned rows app-side to match the input ids order (collect into a map[id]row, emit in input order). Drop the lib/pq import from both files. Verify on both drivers.

These currently fail at runtime on SQLite with 'no such function: ANY' / 'no such function: array_position', contributing to TestGetRelatedCards_Success and the fact-link handler failures. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.
acceptance_criteria: handlers/facts.go and handlers/entity.go run unchanged on Postgres and SQLite; pq.Array removed from both; the similar-facts / similar-entities result order matches the input ids; lib/pq import dropped from both files; relevant handler tests green on SQLite.

title: Phase 6a: run full Go test suite green against SQLite (rewrite tests/conftest.go PG-isms)
description:
Execute docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md Phase 6a. Goal: `go test ./...` green with NO Postgres running -- the test suite defaults to an in-memory SQLite DB built from the consolidated schema.

Scope of conftest.go changes (verified by reading the file):
1. setTestEnvironmentVariables: default DB_DRIVER=sqlite + SQLITE_PATH=:memory: (override with DB_DRIVER=postgres to keep the PG path). Mirror bootstrap.InitServer's driver selection.
2. Setup(): branch on cfg.Database.Driver -- OpenSQLite(:memory:) vs ConnectToDatabase; SchemaDir=.../schema/sqlite for sqlite (so RunMigrations loads schema.sqlite.sql via the Phase 1 splitter); set S.Driver; SKIP the PG-only ResetDatabase on sqlite (it CASCADE/SERIAL -- the :memory: DB is fresh each run).
3. importTestData: the line `SELECT setval('entities_id_seq', ...)` (line ~503) is PG-only -- guard on driver. On SQLite, explicit-id inserts into entities auto-advance AUTOINCREMENT/max-rowid, so no manual reset is needed (no collision).
4. truncateTestData() is DEAD CODE (grep confirms zero callers) -- tx-per-test rollback (Teardown) handles all isolation. Leave as-is; out of scope.

The long tail: Phase 3 swept NON-TEST Go only, so individual *_test.go files across handlers/ and services/ still contain PG-isms (TRUNCATE, setval, ARRAY, ::, etc.) that will surface once the suite runs on SQLite. Iterate to green.

Lean on the existing tx-per-test rollback -- rolled-back transactions never commit, so there is nothing to reset per test.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j. Builds on the closed Phase 1/2/3/5 work.
acceptance_criteria: `go test ./...` exits green from a clean checkout with no Postgres process running (DB_DRIVER unset -> sqlite default). The existing PG test path still works if DB_DRIVER=postgres is set.
notes:
IN PROGRESS 2026-07-26: 12/14 Go packages green vs SQLite (no PG). Only handlers remains: 11 failing tests (down from a 600s deadlock). Committed as b2532498.

Remaining 11 handlers failures (clusters):
- Card-ID generation (3): TestGetNextRootCardID{,Route}, TestGetNextChildCardID -- 'expected ID 11, got 1'; MAX(id)+1 / sequence semantics under test-data reduction.
- TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags (3) -- card/fact/relation paths.
- RSS (3): Test{Star,Unstar,ListStarred}RSSArticleRoute -- 'Failed to create test feed: status 400'.
- TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess (1) -- login 401 after reset (pool write vs test tx visibility).
- TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess (1) -- 'Failed to get preferences'.

Known production-code PG-isms still unfixed (tracked in Zettelgarden-j8q): handlers/facts.go:808 + handlers/entity.go:1141 still use '= ANY($1)' + 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' + pq.Array -- need IN(...) expansion via models.InList/IntArgs + app-side reorder. See status doc 'Phase 6a progress'.

title: SQLite boot wiring: create SQLITE_PATH parent dir + RunMigrations integration test
description:
Two leftover items flagged in the Phase 2 hotfix (docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-status.md), to be done before the first real DB_DRIVER=sqlite run:

1. OpenSQLite (server/sqlite.go) does not yet create the SQLITE_PATH parent directory. Default SQLITE_PATH is ./data/zettelgarden.db, which requires ./data/ to exist -- otherwise first boot fails. MkdirAll the parent dir before opening.

2. No test exercises the real RunMigrations against ./schema/sqlite. Add an integration test that boots an in-memory (or temp file) SQLite, runs RunMigrations pointed at the consolidated schema dir, and asserts the schema loaded (e.g. a known table exists, foreign_key_check passes).

This unblocks Phase 5 work and the first real DB_DRIVER=sqlite boot.
notes:
Done. (1) OpenSQLite now MkdirAlls the SQLITE_PATH parent dir (TestOpenSQLiteCreatesParentDir). (2) Added TestRunMigrationsAppliesConsolidatedSchema exercising real ./schema/sqlite end-to-end (core tables, exactly 1 migration recorded, foreign_key_check clean).

LATENT BOOT BUG FOUND + FIXED: the integration test surfaced that the consolidated schema declared a 'migrations' table identical to the one RunMigrations bootstraps -> first DB_DRIVER=sqlite boot would fatal 'table migrations already exists'. Fixed by making the runner own that table: translate.py now carries RUNNER_OWNED_TABLES={'migrations'} skip-set (regenerated schema.sqlite.sql, clean 6-line diff, 73->72 tables). Also RunMigrations now skips .go files under SchemaDir (schema/sqlite/ co-locates the schema with its Go tests). End-to-end boot smoke (OpenSQLite + RunMigrations against ./schema/sqlite) verified.

Also audit UTC normalization per D5. Independent of Phase 2's consolidated schema -- can proceed now.

title: Phase 2: Consolidated SQLite schema
description:
Produce go-backend/schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql representing the current final-state schema, derived from a pg_dump --schema-only of the live dev DB and adapted to SQLite. Loads cleanly into a fresh :memory: DB via the Phase 1 statement splitter; PRAGMA foreign_key_check passes. See docs/plans/2026-07-17-postgres-to-sqlite-migration-design.md Phase 2.

## Context
BLOCKED on Nick providing pg_dump --schema-only of live dev DB. Until then, can proceed table-by-table from migration files (the spike mini-schema did this for cards). Phase 1 (Zettelgarden-2u2) is done; Phase 3 query translation (~1 day, placeholder sweep eliminated) follows this. Bulk-timing probe confirmed modernc inserts 15k cards in 780ms so ETL stays pure-Go.
acceptance_criteria: Translation rules (proven on cards sub-graph by services/testdata/spike_cards.sqlite.sql): SERIAL/BIGSERIAL -> INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT; TIMESTAMP[TZ] -> DATETIME (NOT TEXT, per D5 -- modernc needs the declared type to return time.Time); JSONB -> TEXT; 2 array columns (notifications.filter_tags, chat_messages.referenced_cards) -> TEXT (JSON); 97 timestamp defaults (58 DEFAULT NOW() + 39 DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) -> DEFAULT (datetime('now')); drop COMMENT ON; drop all 3 GIN indexes (FTS to_tsvector + JSONB containment + array containment -- verified dead, no Go reads them); add CREATE INDEX equivalents for ordinary lookups. Validate: schema loads into :memory: via splitter with zero errors and PRAGMA foreign_key_check passes.
close_reason: Phase 2 done 2026-07-25: consolidated SQLite schema generated (schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql, 73 tables / 134 indexes) via translate.py from the pg_dump snapshot. Loads into :memory: via the Phase 1 splitter; PRAGMA foreign_key_check + integrity_check green (TestConsolidatedSchemaLoads). 3 dead GIN indexes dropped; triggers/functions/comments omitted (Phase 5). Timestamp columns declared DATETIME (D5).

title: Phase 5 follow-up: collapse N+1 in syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate (services/rss_notifications.go)
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/rss_notifications.go syncRSSArticleNotificationsByPredicate() (used by MarkRSSFeedAsRead and MarkRSSFolderAsRead in services/rss.go) issues one GetRSSArticleByID SELECT per matched article -- an N+1. The original PG trigger had the full row in hand and fired once per row, so this is a small perf regression. Acceptable at single-user scale, but a large feed/folder mark-read would feel it.

Fix is small: change the helper to SELECT the full rss_articles columns (not just id) in its single predicate query, hydrate models.RSSArticle directly, and call SyncRSSArticleNotification without the per-row GetRSSArticleByID round-trip. Keep it best-effort (log + continue).

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: MarkRSSFeedAsRead / MarkRSSFolderAsRead issue exactly 1 SELECT for the article set (no per-row GetRSSArticleByID); notification sync behaviour unchanged; existing rss_notifications_sqlite_test.go still green.

title: Phase 7a: drop or modernize PG-only ResetDatabase in server/database.go
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 1-5 SQLite review (2026-07-26). server/database.go ResetDatabase() is still fully PG-specific: CASCADE on every DROP TABLE, SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, DROP TABLE ... CASCADE, etc. It is NOT on the SQLite code path (SQLite uses bootstrap + RunMigrations), so it is harmless today, but it is a latent inconsistency that will confuse readers post-cutover.

Action: as part of Phase 7a (cleanup & rollout), either (a) delete ResetDatabase entirely if nothing calls it on the SQLite path, or (b) gate it on S.Driver == 'postgres' and add a SQLite equivalent (or a no-op). While there, confirm no callers remain that assume PG semantics.

Not a blocker for Phase 6a. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: ResetDatabase either removed or driver-gated; no PG-only SQL remains on the SQLite boot path; backend still boots on both drivers.

title: file_count in user_stats never decrements (files only soft-deleted)
description:
Pre-existing bug surfaced during SQLite Phase 5 scoping (2026-07-25). The user_stats.file_count counter only ever INCREMENTS: the old PG trigger trg_files_delete fired AFTER DELETE (hard delete), but the Go server only ever soft-deletes files (UPDATE files SET is_deleted=true in handlers/files.go DeleteFileRoute). So file_count grows monotonically and overcounts over time.

Decision (Nick, 2026-07-25): leave current behavior as-is for now; do NOT fix as part of Phase 5. Track here. When fixing, decrement file_count in the Go files soft-delete path (and consider whether hard-deletes should ever happen).

title: Phase 5 follow-up: harden userstats addAmount $2-twice param reuse against driver version bumps
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/userstats.go addAmount() references $2 twice in one statement (once in VALUES, once in the ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET) and binds a single positional arg. modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0 and lib/pq both correctly bind the same arg to both occurrences (verified by services/userstats_sqlite_test.go which accumulates to ~0.20 llm_cost / 750 revenue), so this works today on both drivers.

The concern is purely future-proofing: reuse of a numbered param is the one construct in the SQLite migration that is most sensitive to a modernc version bump changing how repeated numbered params are bound.

Options if it ever breaks (low priority): (a) bind the amount twice from the caller side ($2 and $3), or (b) switch to a named param via sql.Named. No action needed today -- this issue exists purely as a breadcrumb so a future 'user_stats add failed' after a go.mod bump is diagnosable in seconds.

Not a blocker for anything. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
acceptance_criteria: If a modernc bump ever breaks repeated numbered-param binding, addAmount is updated (bind twice or use sql.Named) and services/userstats_sqlite_test.go confirms both llm_cost and revenue accumulate correctly.
